questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a grand canonical ensemble ($\mu, V, T$), which thermodynamic potential is directly related to the grand partition function $\Xi$ via $-k_B T \ln \Xi$?
questions.explanationEn: In the grand canonical ensemble, the characteristic thermodynamic potential is the grand potential (Landau potential) $\Phi_G = U - TS - \mu N = -PV$, which is directly connected to the grand partition function $\Xi(\mu, V, T)$ through $\Phi_G = -PV = -k_B T \ln \Xi$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a one-dimensional quantum harmonic oscillator with characteristic vibrational temperature $\Theta_v = h\nu/k_B$, taking the ground state ($v = 0$) as the zero of energy, the vibrational partition function $q_v$ is:
questions.explanationEn: When the zero of energy is chosen at the $v = 0$ level, the vibrational energy levels are $\varepsilon_v = v h\nu = v k_B \Theta_v$ for $v = 0, 1, 2, \dots$. Summing the geometric series gives $q_v = \sum_{v=0}^\infty e^{-v\Theta_v/T} = \frac{1}{1 - e^{-\Theta_v/T}}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In terms of the canonical partition function $Q(N, V, T)$, the average internal energy $U$ of a system is given by:
questions.explanationEn: Using $A = -k_B T \ln Q$ and the Gibbs-Helmholtz relation $U = -T^2 \left[\frac{\partial(A/T)}{\partial T}\right]_{N,V} = -T^2 \frac{\partial(-k_B \ln Q)}{\partial T} = k_B T^2 \left(\frac{\partial \ln Q}{\partial T}\right)_{N,V}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: According to the Debye-Hückel limiting law in water at $298\text{ K}$ ($\log_{10}\gamma_\pm = -A|z_+ z_-|\sqrt{I}$), a plot of $\log_{10}\gamma_\pm$ versus $\sqrt{I}$ for $\text{MgSO}_4$ compared to $\text{NaCl}$ has a slope that is:
optionsEn: Four times as steep as that of $\text{NaCl}$
Twice as steep as that of $\text{NaCl}$
Half as steep as that of $\text{NaCl}$
questions.explanationEn: The slope of $\log_{10}\gamma_\pm$ vs $\sqrt{I}$ is $-A|z_+ z_-|$. For $\text{NaCl}$ ($1:1$), $|z_+ z_-| = |(+1)(-1)| = 1$. For $\text{MgSO}_4$ ($2:2$), $|z_+ z_-| = |(+2)(-2)| = 4$. Thus the slope for $\text{MgSO}_4$ is four times as steep as that for $\text{NaCl}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a reversible galvanic cell operating at constant pressure, if the temperature coefficient of the cell EMF is positive, i.e., $\left(\frac{\partial E}{\partial T}\right)_P > 0$, then for the spontaneous cell reaction:
optionsEn: $\Delta_r S > 0$ and the cell absorbs heat from the surroundings during reversible operation
$\Delta_r S < 0$ and the cell releases heat to the surroundings during reversible operation
questions.explanationEn: Since $\Delta_r G = -nFE$ and $\Delta_r S = -\left(\frac{\partial \Delta_r G}{\partial T}\right)_P = nF\left(\frac{\partial E}{\partial T}\right)_P$, a positive temperature coefficient directly implies $\Delta_r S > 0$. During reversible isothermal operation, $q_{\text{rev}} = T\Delta_r S > 0$, so the cell absorbs heat from the surroundings.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about statistical mechanical ensembles is/are CORRECT?
optionsEn: In a microcanonical ($N, V, E$) ensemble, all accessible microstates have equal a priori probability.
In a canonical ($N, V, T$) ensemble, energy fluctuates around the mean value while $N$ and $V$ remain fixed.
In a grand canonical ($\mu, V, T$) ensemble, both energy $E$ and particle number $N$ fluctuate.
In the thermodynamic limit ($N \to \infty$), relative fluctuations in energy $\sigma_E / \langle E \rangle$ in a canonical ensemble diverge to infinity.
questions.explanationEn: The fundamental postulate of equal a priori probabilities applies to the isolated microcanonical ensemble (A). In a canonical ensemble, thermal contact allows energy fluctuations at fixed $N, V$ (B). In a grand canonical ensemble, both $E$ and $N$ fluctuate (C). In the thermodynamic limit, relative energy fluctuations scale as $1/\sqrt{N} \to 0$ (not infinity), so (D) is false.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a galvanic cell written in standard IUPAC notation (anode on left, cathode on right), which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
optionsEn: Oxidation occurs at the left-hand electrode (anode) and reduction occurs at the right-hand electrode (cathode).
$E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = E_{\text{cathode}}^\circ - E_{\text{anode}}^\circ$ (both expressed as standard reduction potentials).
Standard electrode potential $E^\circ$ is an intensive property and does not change when the half-reaction is multiplied by $2$.
If $E_{\text{cell}} > 0$, the reaction quotient $Q$ is greater than the equilibrium constant $K$.
questions.explanationEn: By IUPAC convention, anode (oxidation) is on the left and cathode (reduction) is on the right (A), with $E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = E_R^\circ - E_L^\circ$ (B). Since $E^\circ = -\Delta G^\circ / (nF)$ is a ratio of two extensive quantities, it is intensive (C). When $E_{\text{cell}} > 0$, $\Delta G < 0$, which means $Q < K$ (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An aqueous solution contains $0.10\text{ M NaCl}$, $0.05\text{ M MgCl}_2$, and $0.02\text{ M Na}_2\text{SO}_4$. Assuming complete dissociation, the total ionic strength of the solution (in $\text{M}$, rounded off to two decimal places) is _______.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The standard EMF of the Daniell cell $\text{Zn}(\text{s})|\text{Zn}^{2+}(\text{aq})||\text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq})|\text{Cu}(\text{s})$ at $298\text{ K}$ is $1.10\text{ V}$. Taking $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$, the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta_r G^\circ$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, rounded off to one decimal place) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: For the two-electron cell reaction $\text{Zn}(\text{s}) + \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq}) \to \text{Zn}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Cu}(\text{s})$ ($n = 2$), $\Delta_r G^\circ = -nFE^\circ = -2 \times 96500 \times 1.10\text{ J mol}^{-1} = -212300\text{ J mol}^{-1} = -212.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A conductivity cell filled with $0.1\text{ M KCl}$ solution (specific conductivity $\kappa = 0.01289\text{ S cm}^{-1}$ at $298\text{ K}$) shows a resistance of $100.0\,\Omega$. The cell constant of this cell (in $\text{cm}^{-1}$, rounded off to three decimal places) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The specific conductivity is related to resistance $R$ and cell constant $G^* = l/A$ by $\kappa = \frac{G^*}{R}$. Therefore, $G^* = \kappa R = 0.01289\text{ S cm}^{-1} \times 100.0\,\Omega = 1.289\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For $1\text{ mol}$ of a diatomic ideal gas with vibrational partition function $q_v = \frac{e^{-\Theta_v/(2T)}}{1 - e^{-\Theta_v/T}}$, the molar vibrational internal energy $U_{\text{vib},m}$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Using $U_{\text{vib},m} = RT^2 \frac{\partial \ln q_v}{\partial T}$ with $\ln q_v = -\frac{\Theta_v}{2T} - \ln(1 - e^{-\Theta_v/T})$: differentiating gives $\frac{\partial \ln q_v}{\partial T} = \frac{\Theta_v}{2T^2} + \frac{(\Theta_v/T^2)e^{-\Theta_v/T}}{1 - e^{-\Theta_v/T}} = \frac{\Theta_v}{T^2}\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{e^{\Theta_v/T} - 1}\right)$. Multiplying by $RT^2$ yields $U_{\text{vib},m} = R\Theta_v\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{e^{\Theta_v/T} - 1}\right)$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a canonical ensemble ($N, V, T$), the mean-square fluctuation in total energy, $\langle (\Delta E)^2 \rangle = \langle E^2 \rangle - \langle E \rangle^2$, is directly related to the isochoric heat capacity $C_V$ by:
questions.explanationEn: Differentiating $\langle E \rangle = -\left(\frac{\partial \ln Q}{\partial \beta}\right)_{N,V}$ with respect to $\beta = (k_B T)^{-1}$ gives $\frac{\partial^2 \ln Q}{\partial \beta^2} = \langle E^2 \rangle - \langle E \rangle^2 = -\left(\frac{\partial \langle E \rangle}{\partial \beta}\right)_{N,V}$. Using $\frac{\partial}{\partial \beta} = -k_B T^2 \frac{\partial}{\partial T}$ yields $\langle (\Delta E)^2 \rangle = k_B T^2 \left(\frac{\partial \langle E \rangle}{\partial T}\right)_{N,V} = k_B T^2 C_V$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the high-temperature limit ($k_B T \gg h\nu$), the vibrational partition function $q_v = \frac{1}{1 - e^{-h\nu/(k_B T)}}$ of a 1D harmonic oscillator simplifies to:
questions.explanationEn:
For $x =  rac{h
u}{k_B T} \ll 1$, Taylor expansion gives $e^{-x} \approx 1 - x$, so $1 - e^{-x} \approx x$. Therefore, $q_v =  rac{1}{1 - e^{-h
u/(k_B T)}} \approx  rac{1}{h
u/(k_B T)} =  rac{k_B T}{h
u}$, which matches the classical phase-space integral result.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: When a dilute aqueous mixture of $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is titrated conductometrically with concentrated $\text{NaOH}$, the conductance versus volume of $\text{NaOH}$ plot shows:
optionsEn: Three linear segments: an initial sharp decrease, a gentle increase in the middle, and a final steep increase
Three linear segments: an initial increase, a middle plateau, and a final decrease
questions.explanationEn: First, strong acid $\text{HCl}$ is neutralized (fast $\text{H}^+$ replaced by $\text{Na}^+$), giving a steep downward line up to the first equivalence point. Second, weak acid $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is neutralized to $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$, increasing ion concentration and giving a gentle upward line up to the second equivalence point. Third, excess $\text{NaOH}$ adds fast $\text{OH}^-$ ions, producing a steep upward line.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For the hydrogen concentration cell $\text{Pt}|\text{H}_2(P_1)|\text{HCl}(\text{aq})|\text{H}_2(P_2)|\text{Pt}$ at temperature $T$, the cell reaction is spontaneous ($E_{\text{cell}} > 0$) when:
questions.explanationEn: At the left electrode (anode): $\text{H}_2(P_1) \to 2\text{H}^+ + 2e^-$. At the right electrode (cathode): $2\text{H}^+ + 2e^- \to \text{H}_2(P_2)$. Overall ($n = 2$): $\text{H}_2(P_1) \to \text{H}_2(P_2)$. By Nernst equation ($E^\circ = 0$), $E_{\text{cell}} = -\frac{RT}{2F}\ln\left(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\right) = \frac{RT}{2F}\ln\left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$, which is positive when $P_1 > P_2$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an ideal monoatomic gas of $N$ atoms of mass $m$ in volume $V$ at temperature $T$ (with $g_{\text{elec}} = 1$), which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
optionsEn: The thermal de Broglie wavelength is $\Lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2\pi m k_B T}}$, and $q_{\text{trans}} = \frac{V}{\Lambda^3}$.
The average translational kinetic energy is $U = \frac{3}{2} N k_B T$, independent of particle mass $m$.
The molar entropy increases with increasing atomic mass $m$ at fixed $T$ and $P$.
The Helmholtz free energy $A$ is independent of the atomic mass $m$.
questions.explanationEn: By definition, $\Lambda = h/\sqrt{2\pi m k_B T}$ and $q_{\text{trans}} = V/\Lambda^3$ (A). Differentiating $\ln Q$ gives $U = \frac{3}{2}N k_B T$, independent of $m$ (B). Since $q_{\text{trans}} \propto m^{3/2}$, $S$ increases as $\frac{3}{2}R\ln m$ (C), and $A = -k_B T\ln Q$ explicitly depends on $m$ via $-\frac{3}{2}N k_B T\ln m$ (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding ionic strength $I$ and activity coefficients in aqueous solutions at $298\text{ K}$ is/are CORRECT?
optionsEn: For a $1:1$ electrolyte of molality $m$, $I = m$.
For a $2:1$ or $1:2$ electrolyte (such as $\text{CaCl}_2$ or $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$) of molality $m$, $I = 3m$.
For a $2:2$ electrolyte (such as $\text{MgSO}_4$) of molality $m$, $I = 4m$.
Adding an inert salt like $\text{KNO}_3$ to a saturated solution of $\text{AgCl}$ decreases the solubility of $\text{AgCl}$.
questions.explanationEn: Computing $I = \frac{1}{2}\sum m_i z_i^2$: for $1:1$, $I = \frac{1}{2}(m + m) = m$ (A); for $2:1$, $I = \frac{1}{2}(4m + 2m) = 3m$ (B); for $2:2$, $I = \frac{1}{2}(4m + 4m) = 4m$ (C). Adding an inert salt increases $I$, which lowers $\gamma_\pm$ of $\text{AgCl}$; since $K_{sp} = s^2 \gamma_\pm^2$ is constant, the solubility $s = \sqrt{K_{sp}}/\gamma_\pm$ INCREASES (salting-in effect, so D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding electrode potentials and thermodynamic parameters is/are CORRECT?
optionsEn: In a Frost diagram (plotting $nE^\circ$ vs oxidation state $N$), a species lying above the line connecting its two adjacent oxidation states is thermodynamically unstable toward disproportionation.
The slope of the line connecting any two points in a Frost diagram equals the standard reduction potential $E^\circ$ of that redox couple.
For a galvanic cell, $\Delta_r H = -nF\left[E - T\left(\frac{\partial E}{\partial T}\right)_P\right]$.
If two half-reactions are added to form a third half-reaction, their $E^\circ$ values are always directly additive regardless of the numbers of electrons transferred.
questions.explanationEn: In a Frost diagram, $nE^\circ = -\Delta G^\circ/F$ vs $N$, so convex-upward points (lying above the chord between neighbors) spontaneously disproportionate (A), and the slope between two states is $\frac{n_2 E_2^\circ - n_1 E_1^\circ}{n_2 - n_1} = E_{2,1}^\circ$ (B). From Gibbs-Helmholtz, $\Delta_r H = -nF[E - T(\partial E/\partial T)_P]$ (C). Because $\Delta G^\circ$ (not $E^\circ$) is additive, $E^\circ$ values must be weighted by $n$ when combining half-reactions (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For $\text{N}_2(\text{g})$, the characteristic rotational temperature is $\Theta_{\text{rot}} = 2.88\text{ K}$ and the symmetry number is $\sigma = 2$. Using the high-temperature classical approximation, the molar rotational entropy $S_{\text{rot},m}$ of $\text{N}_2$ at $300\text{ K}$ (in $\text{J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, rounded off to two decimal places) is _______. (Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.explanationEn: In the high-temperature limit, $q_{\text{rot}} = \frac{T}{\sigma \Theta_{\text{rot}}} = \frac{300}{2 \times 2.88} = 52.0833$. Since $U_{\text{rot},m} = RT$, the molar rotational entropy is $S_{\text{rot},m} = R(1 + \ln q_{\text{rot}}) = 8.314(1 + \ln 52.0833) = 8.314(1 + 3.9528) = 41.18\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Statistical Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: At $298\text{ K}$, a $0.020\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of a weak monoprotic acid $\text{HA}$ has a molar conductivity of $19.5\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$, while its limiting molar conductivity is $\Lambda_m^\circ = 390.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$. The acid dissociation constant $K_a$ is _______ $\times 10^{-5}\text{ M}$ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: The degree of dissociation is $\alpha = \frac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ} = \frac{19.5}{390.0} = 0.050$. By Ostwald's dilution law, $K_a = \frac{c\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha} = \frac{0.020 \times (0.050)^2}{1 - 0.050} = \frac{5.0 \times 10^{-5}}{0.95} = 5.26 \times 10^{-5}\text{ M}$.
